label: KitCommerce vs Dukaan
summary: A quick-start Indian store builder with a free plan and a service fee on every sale — against two MIT projects with no fee and more work up front.
title: KitCommerce vs Dukaan — GoCommerce and Svelte Commerce Compared With Dukaan
description: Dukaan compared with GoCommerce and Svelte Commerce: INR plan prices, Dukaan’s service fee on sales, what that fee comes to at ₹5 lakh a month, payment gateways, shipping, mobile apps and code access — and where Dukaan is the better choice.
ogDescription: Dukaan starts free and takes a service fee as you sell. GoCommerce takes nothing per sale and asks for a developer. Sourced.
h1: Dukaan is free to start and charges as you sell. GoCommerce is the other way round.
lede: Dukaan gets a store online from the web or its Android and iOS apps, with a free plan — then takes a service fee of 0.99% to 4.99% of sales, by plan, on top of the payment gateway’s charge. GoCommerce and Svelte Commerce take nothing per sale, and ask for a server and a developer before the first one.

glanceLede: Dukaan’s side is taken from its pricing page — plan cards, comparison table and FAQ — linked at the foot of this page. Ours is what GoCommerce and Svelte Commerce do today.
rows: A hosted store builder, run from the web or Dukaan’s Android and iOS apps on every plan.
Two MIT projects you deploy: GoCommerce for the backend and a web admin, Svelte Commerce for the storefront.
Free; Starter ₹299, Growth ₹999 and Infinity ₹5,999 a month billed monthly — or ₹2,500, ₹8,000 and ₹50,000 billed yearly.
4.99% on Free, 3.99% on Starter, 1.99% on Growth and 0.99% on Infinity — capped at ₹200 an order, not charged on manual orders, and on top of gateway charges.
Nine payment modules, Razorpay and Stripe among them; cash on delivery is the core’s default method.
Dukaan Delivery built in; Shiprocket and Shippo, or your own Blue Dart, Delhivery, DTDC or Xpressbees account.
Shiprocket, Delhivery and NimbusPost modules book shipments; India Post consignments are recorded; Shippo, ShipStation and others for parcels abroad.
1 store on Free and Starter, 3 on Growth, 10 on Infinity; 1, 2, 5 and 20 staff accounts.
Channels for several storefronts and roles for staff, with no count set by a plan.
Themes from Dukaan’s marketplace, and a code editor for fonts, colours and theme sections.
The source — storefront, checkout and backend.
Imports catalogues from Shopify, WooCommerce, Gumroad or a CSV file, and can keep your old URL structure.
Imports a whole Shopify catalogue, safely re-runnable; from anything else, a script against the documented API.
Dukaan’s Android and iOS apps, on every plan.
No app. The admin is a web app compiled into the GoCommerce binary.
Yours — a single Go binary beside a PostgreSQL database, on any server you choose.
Dukaan says it is tailored to online businesses that depend on repeat purchases.
Stores with a developer, and developers building stores for others.

cost.note: Arithmetic from Dukaan’s plan table. Growth and Infinity cost the same at exactly this volume; above it, Infinity’s lower fee wins. The ₹200 cap bites only on large orders — on Growth, above about ₹10,050 an order. The gateway’s own charge is paid on both sides and left out; Razorpay lists 2% + GST. Dukaan’s FAQ, on the same page, quotes different rates for differently named plans; we have used the plan table.

themWhen: You want to start selling today for ₹0, from your phone, and pay only once sales come in.
Your sales are small, so a few per cent of them costs less than paying someone to run a server.
You want delivery, payments and the store in one place, with no code at all.
You are testing a product idea and may not need a store in six months.
usWhen: Your sales have grown to where Dukaan’s fee is a real line — ₹10,949 a month at ₹5 lakh, on its cheapest plan for that volume.
You want to change the checkout and the order flow, not only the theme.
You want your store’s data in a database you control, under software with an MIT licence.
You have, or can hire, a developer — the one cost GoCommerce cannot remove.
takeOnExtra: No phone app to run the store from — the admin is a web app.
No built-in delivery service: you bring your own Shiprocket, Delhivery or NimbusPost account.

faq.q: Does Dukaan charge a fee on sales?
faq.a: Yes. Dukaan’s plan table lists a service fee of 4.99% on Free, 3.99% on Starter, 1.99% on Growth and 0.99% on Infinity, capped at ₹200 an order and not charged on manual orders. Its FAQ adds that the fee is exclusive of payment gateway charges. GoCommerce charges no fee on sales.
Free is ₹0. Starter is ₹299, Growth ₹999 and Infinity ₹5,999 a month billed monthly, or ₹2,500, ₹8,000 and ₹50,000 billed yearly, on Dukaan’s pricing page.

faq.q: Which payment gateways work on each?
faq.a: Dukaan lists Cashfree, Razorpay, PayPal and Stripe. GoCommerce has nine payment modules, Razorpay and Stripe among them, and cash on delivery in the core; Cashfree and PayPal are not among its modules.

faq.q: Can I move from Dukaan to GoCommerce?
faq.a: There is no Dukaan importer, so moving means a script against GoCommerce’s documented API. The one catalogue importer GoCommerce has is for Shopify.

faq.q: Can Svelte Commerce be the storefront for a Dukaan store?
faq.a: No. Dukaan is not among the 26 backends Svelte Commerce connects to. Svelte Commerce reaches GoCommerce through an early connector, 0.1.0, covering catalogue, cart, checkout and order lookup; customer accounts and search are not covered yet.
